sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Apprehensive; vertigo; head heavy during
menses. Eyes burn, noises in ears.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Frequent eructations, tasting like bad
eggs. Rising of water in mouth.

sections.label: Urinary
sections.text:
Stitches and burning in the orifice of the
urethra after urinating. Stream intermits and dribbles.
The urine passed in the morning copious, bright yellow,
soon becomes turbid, and deposits a copious red sedi-
ment. The urine is greenish as passed; is of a clear
color, and in a large quantity. Diabetes. [Phos. ac.;
Lad. ac.; Ars. brom.]

sections.label: Female
sections.text:
Thick leucorrhcea, as profuse as the menses,
witn AA'eary pain in the small of the back and thighs,
on moving about. Some blood from the vagina between
the menses. Menstruation returned after fourteen days ;
the discharge was thick, black, and profuse. Menses
too early, intermit.

Neck and Back. — Bruised and ulcerative pain be-
tween the shoulders, with a feeling as oi a lump as
large as the fist, on which account she could not lie
upon her back or side; relieved by rubbing. Violent
pain in the small of the back, as if bruised, and as be-
fore menstruation.

Extnemities. — The left arm and foot fall asleep in
bed, ip the morning after waking.

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
Small pimples over the whole body, that itch
violently. Suppressed itch. \Sulph.] Crawling in the
tips of the fingers of the left hand; better on rubbing.
Warts. Erysipelas (applied locally as a saturated solu-
tion).

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chill from Q to 10 a. m. Shuddering in
back; heat in one part and chill in another.

Oppression of chest, with burning in chest when walking.
^^ Burning in middle of chest; under upper part of sternum.

rising, with great sensitiveness to touch, > by walking.

seventh day),’. — Appetite diminished (eighth day),*. — Little appetite (tenth

thirteenth days),’. — Entire loss of appetite, aversion to warm food ; bread
seems to agree best,’. — No hunger, yet she relishes her food, though she will
not eat meat (twelfth day),’. — [130.] No hunger nor appetite ; yet no aver-
sion to food,’. — Aversion to ail food, even when thinking of it (second day),’.
— Aversion to all food that she thinks of, till evening, when she had nausea,
but was able to eat,’. — Tobacco was not relished (eighth day),*. — Aversion
to tobacco (tenth day),*. — No desire for smoking (ninth and twelfth days),*.
— Thirst. Thirst in the morning after rising, disappearing after break-
fast (third and fourth days),’.— Thirst in the evening, for several days,

eructations, followed by taste of the food eatoi the previous day (soon),*.—
